The way Voat currently looks looks like a web forum from the mid 2000's, which, yeah, is when Reddit was made.

There's a lot of things I'd want to change, mainly, how busy the sites design is. There are a lot of features people don't use, and I believe those should be moved behind context sensitive menus. For example, instead of having the buttons "Front - All -Random" next to each other, small, and available on every page, instead, it should be a drop down menu saying "Front| v |" and when you click on the down arrow, it gives you the options for All and Random. The button should also be larger and outlined. UX changes like this will pave way to a universal design that would work on phones and tablets easily as well as PC.

Other little things would include moving the top bar and pinning it permanently to the left, which is generally wasted space on every single Voat page. And/or move the "My Subverses" dropdown and pin it with a "| < |" so that you can make your subverses appear and disappear as needed. UX changes like this would make Voat significantly more modern, and feel familiar enough that a reddit user could jump in easily but fresh enough that new users will see it's usability benefits in comparison to the competition.
